risks.description: POST /approve may apply the durable approval+payment effect and then fail to acknowledge within a sane client timeout, so the caller cannot tell whether the approval landed. Every already-covered scenario timed out on exactly this call and none inspected the store afterward, so the effect's actual status is unverified.
risks.basis: Prior failures C01-C04 (all POST /approve timed out); AC-APPROVAL-001 (approval must be recorded durably).

risks.description: An approval that returns success may never be written to the durable store, so a re-read of persisted state (state.py, a fresh process) still shows pending while the API claims approved.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 (records the approval durably); diff touches r5/fixture/app.py approval path.

risks.description: Approval state may not survive a restart / independent re-read of the persisted store, violating the durability promise.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 (approval state survives a re-read of persisted state).

risks.description: Two approvals arriving simultaneously for the same invoice may each apply the payment effect, producing a double payment even though sequential idempotency is already covered.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 (records the approval durably); concurrency is untested (only sequential idempotency covered).

scenarios.title: Timed-out approve leaves an ambiguous durable effect
scenarios.purpose: Determine whether a POST /approve that fails to answer within a sane client timeout has nonetheless landed the approval in the durable store, which is the exact blind spot behind every prior timed-out scenario.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a unique invoice id (W2A) created on first touch; asserts only against W2A rows in the store, so it cannot read or clobber another scenario's records. Shares the single store file/api service, so it must not run concurrently with other r5-store scenarios.
scenarios.rationale: The three covered scenarios all asserted status==200 and timed out; none inspected the store, so whether the effect actually happened is unknown. A durable read after a bounded-timeout request settles the ambiguity.
expected_observations: POST /approve returns 200 with an approved acknowledgement within the 3s client timeout
The durable store (state.py W2A) reports W2A status=approved, matching the acknowledgement
forbidden_observations: The client receives no successful response within the timeout while state.py W2A already shows status=approved (a silent, ambiguous effect the caller cannot confirm)

scenarios.title: Approve acknowledged by API but absent from durable store
scenarios.purpose: Detect divergence between what the approval endpoint reports (in-memory/HTTP response) and what a re-read of the durable store shows.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a unique invoice id (W2C) created on first touch and asserts only against W2C; shares the store file/api service so it must be serialized with other r5-store scenarios.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires the approval to be recorded durably, not merely reflected in a response body. Comparing the API's own read of the invoice against the file-backed oracle exposes a response that lies about persistence.
expected_observations: The API GET of W2C reports approved AND state.py W2C reports status=approved (response and durable store agree)
forbidden_observations: The API reports W2C approved while the durable store (state.py W2C) still shows status=pending

scenarios.title: Approval survives an api restart / independent re-read
scenarios.purpose: Verify that an approval recorded before a service restart is still present when the persisted store is re-read afterward, per the durability-across-re-read promise.
scenarios.isolation_note: This scenario restarts the api service, which reinitializes the shared store; it is destructive to every other r5-store scenario and MUST run in isolation (serialized) from all of them. It uses invoice id W2B.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-002 promises approval state survives a re-read of persisted state. A restart is the strongest form of independent re-read: it proves the approval is on disk and not merely in a process's memory.
expected_observations: Before restart, state.py W2B shows status=approved
After the api restart, state.py W2B still shows status=approved
forbidden_observations: After restart the approval is gone: state.py W2B no longer shows status=approved, shows status=pending, or the store is reset/missing

scenarios.title: Simultaneous approvals of one invoice pay exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise two approvals racing on the same invoice at the same instant and confirm the durable store records a single payment, distinct from the already-covered sequential idempotency case.
scenarios.isolation_note: Issues its two racing requests against a unique invoice id (W2D) and asserts only against W2D; shares the store file/api service so it must be serialized with other r5-store scenarios.
scenarios.rationale: Covered idempotency is sequential (approve twice in order). A genuine race can slip past a check-then-write gap under locking, producing a double payment that sequential tests never reveal. The durable payment count is the oracle.
expected_observations: After two simultaneous approvals, state.py W2D shows status=approved with payments=1
forbidden_observations: state.py W2D shows payments=2 (or more) after the concurrent approvals — the invoice was paid twice

assumptions: The current run exhibits the stalling/timeout behavior (every prior POST /approve timed out), so bounded client timeouts plus a durable-store read are the reliable oracle; the state.py CLI reads the on-disk store, not the running process.
Invoices are created on first touch, so each scenario can safely use its own unique invoice id (W2A/W2B/W2C/W2D) without seeding.
state.py accepts an invoice id as an extra argument to scope its output to one record.
Restarting the api service reinitializes the shared store, making the restart scenario destructive and requiring serialization with all other r5-store scenarios.
unresolved_questions: The acceptance criteria do not state a maximum acknowledgement latency for POST /approve, so it is unspecified whether an approval that lands durably but answers slowly (or times out) counts as a pass or a defect; the ambiguous-effect scenario flags the divergence but the intended contract needs confirmation.

Neither AC names concurrency or double-payment protection explicitly; AC-APPROVAL-001 ('records the approval durably') is the closest anchor, but whether 'exactly one payment per invoice' is a promised invariant should be confirmed with the founder.
AC-APPROVAL-002 says state survives a 're-read of persisted state' but does not clarify whether a full process restart is in scope; the restart scenario assumes it is.
